description.text: Healthpeak Properties, Inc. is a Standard & Poor’s (“S&P”) 500 company that owns, operates, and develops high-quality real estate focused on healthcare discovery and delivery in the United States (“U.S.”). Our company was originally founded in 1985. We are organized as an umbrella partnership REIT (“UPREIT”). We hold substantially all of our assets and conduct our operations through our operating subsidiary, Healthpeak OP, a consolidated subsidiary of which we are the managing member. We are a Maryland corporation and qualify as a self-administered REIT. We are headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with additional corporate offices in California, Tennessee, Wisconsin, and Massachusetts and property management offices in several locations throughout the U.S. We have a diversified portfolio of high-quality healthcare properties across three core asset classes of outpatient medical, lab, and senior housing real estate. Under the outpatient medical and lab segments, we own, operate, and develop outpatient medical buildings, hospitals, and lab buildings. Under the senior housing segment, our properties are operated through RIDEA structures. We have other non-reportable segments that are comprised primarily of: (i) loans receivable, (ii) a preferred equity investment, and (iii) three other properties. These non-reportable segments have been presented on a combined basis herein. On March 1, 2024 (the “Closing Date”), we completed our merger with Physicians Realty Trust (the “Merger”).

about.description_short: Healthpeak Properties, Inc. is a fully integrated real estate investment trust (REIT) and S&P 500 company. Healthpeak owns, operates, and develops high-quality real estate focused on healthcare discovery and delivery.

analysis_md:
# DOC — Healthpeak Properties, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-17. Price $18.98 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap (est) $13.211B — in scope under $40B. **Sector model misfit (Real Estate): every engine figure below is read with that warning attached; the verdict is cross-checked on the REIT-native FFO/AFFO basis in Thoughts.**

All figures are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or the cited Q2 2026 reporting — none are recomputed.

## What it is
A fully integrated healthcare REIT (S&P 500, SIC 6798): outpatient medical buildings, lab / life-science buildings, and senior housing (the Janus Living platform, IPO'd in 2026 with Healthpeak retaining control). On March 1, 2024 it completed its merger with Physicians Realty Trust, adding 299 outpatient medical buildings — the event that breaks the per-share history (see DILUTION). Q2 2026 (release, Aug 4, 2026): total revenues $771.6M (+11.1% YoY, helped by senior-housing consolidation), FFO as Adjusted $0.46/share — flat YoY; same-store adjusted NOI +1.8% (lab −3.2%); outpatient occupancy 90.7%, lab occupancy 78.5%; full-year 2026 FFO as Adjusted guidance raised twice to $1.73–$1.77/share.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,251,959,000; capex (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets — development, redevelopment and other major improvements, i.e. mostly *growth* capex for a REIT) $894,949,000; SBC $14,410,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $342,600,000 = $0.49/share** (latest FY OE/share, key_numbers.md).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $235,263,000 total in FY2025 — lower than the conservative figure, because FY2025 net income was only $71,347,000 (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE). Neither REIT-inappropriate series is the native yardstick: the company reports FFO as Adjusted of $1.73–$1.77/share guided for 2026, and external reporting puts FY2025 AFFO at ~$1.69/share with a 72% dividend payout. The engine charges *all* development capex against OE, which is why its OE/share ($0.47–0.49) sits far below AFFO — the core of the sector misfit, and the reason the IVs below are model artifacts, not entry points.
- OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (negative in the merger/COVID-era trough years of the longer history: OE/share −$0.09 in FY2020, −$0.16 in FY2022 on the filed history). Net debt $9.380B (key_numbers.md; basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt). On the company's own leverage yardstick, net debt / adjusted EBITDAre was 4.7x at Q2 2026 — the balance sheet is investment-grade (BBB+/Baa1), not distressed; the engine's 28.64x is net debt over its capex-charged OE, not over property cash flow.
- Dividend: DPS TTM $1.22 (fundamentals.json) = a 6.4% yield at $18.98 on the engine price; last dividend cut FY2021; buybacks resumed in 2026 ($100M at $16.81 in Q2, new $500M authorization; dividends paid TTM $845,985,000 and buybacks TTM $101,665,000 per fundamentals.json).

**Base used = normalized (median of last 3 FY OE/share) $0.47/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The TTM alternative was attempted and is not available filing-direct: `ttm.py DOC` exits non-zero ("capex: no post-FY YTD fact — no 10-Q since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end" under the capex tag it reads), and fundamentals.json's TTM block (through 2026-06-30) likewise carries capex as null while reporting TTM revenue $2,949,806,000 (+5.52% YoY), OCF $1,231,026,000, net income $243,297,000, SBC $17,353,000 and D&A $1,097,527,000 on 693,731,899 duration-weighted diluted shares. With no filing-direct TTM capex leg, no TTM base was constructed and no override was declared — the median base stands, and the staleness is disclosed rather than papered over.
Revenue-basis note: the engine's revenue series is the contract-revenue component tag, not the filer's total (fundamentals.json warns its own total — FY2025 revenue $2,822,512,000 — exceeds the contract-revenue line, which is a component for this filer). The blend's revenue CAGRs (5y 6.71%, 3y 6.86%) are therefore component-basis; the filer's-total TTM growth of +5.52% is the cleaner cross-check and points the same direction.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-moderate
Justification: scarce on-/near-campus outpatient locations, health-system relationships and post-merger scale are real but replicable with capital; there is no pricing power beyond contractual escalators. The measured history argues against more: the `roic_proxy` series in fundamentals.json is null for every year (the filer tags no operating-income line the proxy needs, so no ROIC evidence can be quoted — itself a reason not to award a high moat on faith), gross margin ran 58.1% / 58.6% / 60.2% in FY2022–24 (fundamentals.json annual) with no expansion, OE/share fell from $1.57 (FY2016) to $0.49 (FY2025), Q2 2026 FFO as Adjusted was flat YoY, and lab occupancy is 78.5%.
- FOR: scarce healthcare locations (on/near hospital campuses, core lab clusters) that are supply-constrained and slow to replicate; health-system relationships and scale — the Physicians Realty merger made it one of the largest outpatient medical landlords, and Q2 2026 executed 1.6M sq ft of new/renewal leases at 90.7% outpatient occupancy; long leases with contractual escalators and a rent roll diversified across outpatient, lab and senior housing (Janus Living revenue +45% YoY in Q2 2026); investment-grade balance sheet with 4.7x net debt / adjusted EBITDAre and proven capital-recycling access ($1.025B Brookfield outpatient JV recap, July 2026).
- AGAINST: no structural pricing power — rent resets to local market supply/demand and tenants can relocate; lab oversupply (occupancy 78.5%, same-store lab NOI −3.2% YoY) whose recovery depends on biotech funding, not Healthpeak; a weak through-cycle per-share record (OE/share $1.57 → $0.49, FY2021 dividend cut, DPS $2.10 in FY2016 vs $1.22 TTM); leverage/rate exposure — REIT values are hostage to cap rates and refinancing costs.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4.0 final run (2026-10-17)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine blend is 1.79% (rev CAGR 5y 6.71%, 3y 6.86%, latest YoY 6.25% — all cut by the −5.00pp share-count adjustment — plus an OE/share CAGR 2y of 26.91% that is an artifact of the depressed merger-era base and was *not* allowed to set the starts). Against actual prints — TTM total revenue +5.52% YoY, Q2 2026 same-store NOI +1.8%, FFO as Adjusted flat YoY at $0.46, 2026 FFO guidance $1.73–$1.77 vs a ~$1.84 FY2025 level in external reporting — per-share cash growth of ~0–2% is what the company is actually printing. The base start therefore stays at the blend's 1.8%, and the bull starts were recalibrated *down* from the default offsets (super bull would have started at 13.8%, above any per-share print the company has produced): offsets −0.07 / −0.03 / 0.00 / +0.03 / +0.07 give starts of −5.2 / −1.2 / **1.8** / 4.8 / 8.8%. Probabilities were shifted bear-ward per the OE_VOLATILE flag: 15/30/30/15/10 (defaults 10/25/30/25/10). OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $18.98.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -5.2% | 0.75 | Lab occupancy slides further, cap rates widen, refinancing bites | $2.14 | 3.80% |
| Bear | 30% | -1.2% | 0.90 | FFO/share drifts down on lab drag and interest expense | $3.01 | 4.41% |
| Base | 30% | 1.8% | 1.00 | Escalators + outpatient/senior-housing growth offset lab; FFO roughly flat-to-slightly-up | $3.75 | 4.96% |
| Bull | 15% | 4.8% | 1.10 | Lab commencements outrun expirations, Janus scales, recycling accretes | $4.63 | 5.61% |
| Super bull | 10% | 8.8% | 1.25 | Lab recovery + distressed life-science acquisitions at wide spreads | $6.13 | 6.70% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $3.66 (−80.7% vs price), IV@12% $4.81, IV@10% $6.09, weighted IRR 4.90%, base-case IRR 4.96%**
- **Tier by numbers: D — and the bear and bull tiers are both D** (IRR band 4.41% → 5.61%; full scenario range 3.80%–6.70%), so there is no TIER_BAND sizing question. Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 2.48%, terminal value 17.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 2.86x, net debt 28.64x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 9.5 months ago): ttm.py was run and cannot build a filing-direct TTM — its capex leg has no post-FY YTD fact under the tag it reads, and fundamentals.json's TTM block confirms capex as null while supplying the other TTM legs (quoted under Owner's earnings). The normalized median base is used and the staleness is disclosed; no base override was declared, because a TTM OE built on an invented capex leg would violate the bounded authority (no filing source for the missing leg was located).
- **DILUTION** (share count +8.89%/yr): explained, not ongoing dilution — diluted shares went 547,275,000 (FY2023) → 676,233,000 (FY2024) → 696,044,000 (FY2025) on the filed history because the March 1, 2024 Physicians Realty Trust merger was paid in stock. SBC is trivial ($14,410,000 in FY2025; $17,353,000 TTM per fundamentals.json) and is not the driver. The direction has already reversed: shares outstanding were 689,527,260 at 2026-08-03 (dcf_numbers.json) after $100M of Q2 2026 buybacks, with a new $500M authorization. The −5.00pp growth adjustment is retained as the engine applies it, which is conservative given the merger origin.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real on the filed series (−$0.16 to $0.49 across FY2022–25, with the merger break and development-capex swings inside it). Handled by the normalized median base and by shifting scenario weight bear-ward (45% on bear-or-worse vs 35% in the defaults).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): found and explained — it is the normal REIT non-cash wedge, not a cash-quality problem. FY2025 net income was $71,347,000 against OCF of $1,251,959,000; the FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement reconciles the gap mainly with depreciation and amortization of $1,058,865,000, an equity loss from unconsolidated joint ventures of $173,984,000, partly offset by a $69,488,000 gain on sales of real estate (10-K consolidated statements of cash flows, via search of the filed 10-K). The OCF-based conservative OE is unaffected by the non-cash D&A leg.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Real Estate): accepted in full — confidence is **low**, score.json records model_fit "misfit" and suppresses any alert on that ground. The engine charges all development/redevelopment capex (FY2025: $894,949,000) as if it were maintenance, so its OE and IVs understate REIT economics by construction. The verdict was therefore cross-checked on AFFO (see Thoughts): the D conclusion survives the correction, which is why no tier override was taken.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 28.64x normalized OE): the multiple is an artifact of the same capex-charged OE denominator. The filing-basis picture: total debt $9,847,894,000 less cash $467,457,000 = net debt $9,380,437,000 (financials_history.csv, FY2025; debt basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt, no separate short-term debt tag), against total assets $20,336,018,000 and equity $7,500,094,000; the company's own Q2 2026 yardstick is net debt / adjusted EBITDAre 4.7x with BBB+/Baa1 ratings. Leverage is a real rate/cap-rate sensitivity (stressed in the bear cases) but not a solvency flag at these levels.
- The preliminary run's **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** flag (4.48x) no longer appears in the final run: recalibrating the bull starts down to evidence-based levels narrowed the spread to 2.86x. Confidence is low anyway on the sector misfit, so nothing turns on it.
- Enrichment note (non-blocking): all step-9 enrichment files were written (fundamentals, prices, segments, statements, profile/street, reprice). segments.py reports its business-segment revenue rows sum to 97.0% of the consolidated total for FY2025 (ties_to_total: false) — a segment-table gap in the filing extraction; no score figure uses segment data, so nothing turns on it.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *method range*, and here it is unusually wide because the model is the wrong tool: engine OE basis → weighted IRR 4.90%, IV@15% $3.66. REIT-native basis → FY2025 AFFO ~$1.69/share (external reporting) is an ~8.9% AFFO yield at $18.98, the dividend alone yields 6.4% (DPS TTM $1.22), and per-share FFO is guided essentially flat ($1.73–$1.77 for 2026, FFO as Adjusted flat YoY in Q2 2026). An AFFO-yield-plus-growth total return lands in the high single digits — better than the engine's print, still nowhere near a 15% hurdle. **Both methods agree on the tier; they disagree only on how bad it is.** That agreement is what makes a D verdict safe to record at low confidence.
- What the buyer at $18.98 is actually underwriting: a 6.4% monthly-paid dividend, lab occupancy recovering from 78.5%, Janus Living scaling inside the consolidated group, and capital recycling (Brookfield recap, $1.75B of proceeds year-to-date through Aug 3, 2026 per the Q2 release) funding buybacks below intrinsic value. That is an income-plus-modest-growth proposition, not a 15% compounder, and management's own guidance (flat FFO/share) says so.
- Risks: lab oversupply working off slowly if biotech funding stays tight; senior-housing operating leverage inside Janus; interest expense already rising (Q2 2026 interest $92,280,000 vs $75,063,000 a year earlier in the filed 10-Q); transaction/change-of-control gains flattering 2026 GAAP income (H1 2026 net income includes gains on the SWF senior-housing JV consolidation and an outpatient disposition, per the Q2 2026 release) — none of which changes the cash picture.
- Hurdle math, stated plainly: on engine numbers the stock clears 15% only at $3.66 (20% at $2.62, 25% at $2.04 — key_numbers.md). Those prices are artifacts of charging growth capex to OE and should **not** be quoted as real entry points; on the AFFO basis there is no plausible near-term price-independent path to 15% either, since the starting yield plus guided growth sums to roughly 9–11% even before multiple risk.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 4.90% on the engine basis; high-single-digit expected return on the REIT-native AFFO basis — D under both)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector model misfit by construction; the tier is nonetheless robust because the corrected basis lands in the same tier)
- One-liner: Diversified healthcare REIT, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% on any basis: Tier D, weighted IRR 4.90%, weighted IV@15% $3.66 vs $18.98 on the engine OE base (which charges all development capex), and even on the REIT-native AFFO basis (~$1.69/sh in FY2025 per external reporting, a ~6.4% dividend yield plus ~0–2% per-share growth) the expected return is high-single-digit; it would clear 15% only at the engine hurdle price of $3.66, which the sector model misfit makes a model artifact rather than a real entry point — confidence low.
